sentences.text:
These writ petitions have been filed seeking the relief in the nature of certiorarified mandamus seeking interference with an order of the first respondent, the District Collector, Trichy, and to consequently direct the said first respondent to refer the matters relating to acquisition of lands of the petitioners herein to the appropriate Court, so as to enable the petitioners to get enhanced compensation for the properties acquired.
2.Let me state the facts in W.P(MD)Nos.13274 to 13313 of 2023.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The writ petitioners in these writ petitions have stated that the lands at Kannudaiyanpatti and K.Periyapatti Village (North), Trichy District respectively, had been acquired for industrial purposes by G.O.No. 94(Industries)
Department, dated 14.05.2013.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: It was also published in the Government Order ex-ordinary No.194 dated 22.09.2014.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Notification was issued on 04.09.2014.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Thereafter, G.O.Ms.No.45, dated 14.05.2014, was issued with direction for payment of interim compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Claiming that the stipulations under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, had not been followed, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P(MD)Nos.13313 to 13274 of 2023 the petitioners had presented representation before the District Collector, Trichy to refer the entire issue before the competent Court.

entities.text:

Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The petitioners in these writ petitions had given applications on various dates.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The only issue was with respect to Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
The entire issue arose Section 64 of the said Act, which is extracted hereunder:
64.Reference to Authority.-(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be,
whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Provided that the Collector shall, within a period of thirty days from the date of receipt of application, make a reference to the appropriate Authority:
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Provided further that where the Collector fails to make such reference within the period so specified, the applicant may apply to the Authority, as the case may be,
requesting it to direct the Collector to make the reference to it within a period of thirty days.
Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95595494/
2
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
(2) The application shall state the grounds on which objection to the award is taken:
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P(MD)Nos.13313 to 13274 of 2023
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
Provided that every such application shall be made-- (a) person making it was present or represented before the Collector at the time when he made his award, within six weeks from the date of the Collectors award;
(b) in other cases, within six weeks of the receipt of the notice from the Collector under section 21, or within six months from the date of the Collectors award,
whichever period shall first expire:
Provided further that the Collector may entertain an application after the expiry of the said period, within a further period of one year, if he is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for not filing it within the period specified in the first proviso.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 3.The said provision, gives authority to the Collector to, on receipt of an applications, to make a reference.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Though time limit has been given, there is also a proviso which stipulates that the Collector may entertain the applications after the expiry of the said period and within a further period of one year.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The time limits may be examined by the District Collector in each one of the cases and in each one of the cases that the petitioners give necessary reason for delay and if the District Collector is satisfied with the delay, then the District Collector may refer the matter to the competent Court, then the District Court at Trichy.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P(MD)Nos.13313 to 13274 of 2023
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 4.The learned counsel for the petitioners placed reliance on an earlier order in W.P(MD)No.15207 of 2022, Muthulakshmi and others-vs-The District Collector, Trichy and another.

entities.text: Muthulakshmi and others-vs-The District Collector, Trichy and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: By an order, dated 17.04.2023 in similar issue, this Court had held that in view of this particular provision which had not been examined by the District Collector, the order impugned should be set aside and fresh orders have to be passed.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: The said order has to be passed on the basis of the representations already given.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text:
With respect to the period of limitation, the aforementioned directions may be followed and to avoid any technicalities, a direction is given to the petitioners herein to forward a fresh representations, copy of the original applications afresh, enclosing a copy of this order and if it is so,
within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, then the issue of limitation need not be stressed by the District Collector.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: 5.In view of the above, these writ petitions are allowed.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: No costs.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 19 June, 2023.json

sentences.text: Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.

sentences.text:
The petitioner owned the land comprised in survey no.222/1A situated at Minnampalli Village,
Namakkal Taluk and District.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In the said land, one irrigation well was in existence for irrigation purpose of the said land.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: While being so, the second respondent issued notification under Section 4(1) of Land Acquisition Act (hereinafter called as 'the Act') for formation of Salem-Karur Broad Gauge Railway line in Minnampalli Village of Namakkal Taluk and District.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Enquiry under Section 5 (A) of the Act was dispensed with in view of the urgency clause under Section 17(4) of the Act.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Declaration under Section 6 of the Act was approved and published in the Government gazette.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In order to determine the compensation, the land under acquisition was treated as manavari dry land by the second respondent and the value as compensation was determined at Rs.66,304/- per hectare.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Accordingly on 10.11.1999, award No.16/1999-2000 vide Roc.152/98 Unit-I was passed.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: As per the award, no compensation was awarded for the well situated in the said land.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the petitioner made request for compensation, solatium together with interest for the well situated in the very same land.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, it was rejected on the basis of GO.Ms.No.952 Revenue https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

sentences.text: Hence, the advantage which an agricultural land may have because of the irrigation facility it had from the irrigation well, could only enhance the value of agricultural land depending upon the water yield from the well.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Again when the agricultural land, the irrigation of which was possible from the water of the irrigation well, is acquired, the value of the land so acquired will have to be determined taking into consideration the irrigation facility it had from the well.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: In this situation the irrigation well in an acquired agricultural land, cannot have a value apart from the value of the agricultural land itself....
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 3. On the strength of the above judgment, the Government passed order in GO.Ms.No.952 Revenue Department dated 04.12.1998 thereby ordering that separate compensation needs to be paid to the irrigation wells which are situated in the agricultural lands acquired.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 4. On perusal of the aforementioned judgment and the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 02/01/2026 05:45:30 pm ) Government order, it is revealed that when the compensation was awarded to the agricultural land, taking into consideration the irrigation facility, the irrigation well in such acquired agricultural land cannot have any value apart from the value of agricultural land.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: But in the case on hand, the petitioner's land cannot to be treated as agricultural land with irrigation facility.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, by citing the Government order inGO.Ms.No.952 Revenue Department dated 04.12.1998, the claim of the petitioner was rejected.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, the respondent treated the petitioner's land at par with other adjacent lands which were classified as dry land and the same have no irrigation facilities such as open well or borewell.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the above Government order is not applicable to the land which is classified as dry land.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. Admittedly, the petitioner's land was compensated under the head of dry land.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: As per the award dated 10.11.1999, the subject land was treated as dry land for determining compensation.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Therefore,
the Government order is not at all applicable to the case on hand.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, there is no separate classification as punjai land with irrigation facility or without irrigation facility in the Government order.
sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

sentences._hearing_file: Periyasamy vs The District Collector on 8 October, 2025.json

These writ petitions have been filed seeking the relief in the nature of certiorarified mandamus seeking interference with an order of the first respondent, the District Collector, Trichy, and to consequently direct the said first respondent to refer the matters relating to acquisition of lands of the petitioners herein to the appropriate Court, so as to enable the petitioners to get enhanced compensation for the properties acquired.
2.Let me state the facts in W.P(MD)Nos.13274 to 13313 of 2023.
Notification was issued on 04.09.2014.
Thereafter, G.O.Ms.No.45, dated 14.05.2014, was issued with direction for payment of interim compensation.
Claiming that the stipulations under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, had not been followed, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis W.P(MD)Nos.13313 to 13274 of 2023 the petitioners had presented representation before the District Collector, Trichy to refer the entire issue before the competent Court.
The only issue was with respect to Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The entire issue arose Section 64 of the said Act, which is extracted hereunder:
64.Reference to Authority.-(1) Any person interested who has not accepted the award may, by written application to the Collector, require that the matter be referred by the Collector for the determination of the Authority, as the case may be,
whether his objection be to the measurement of the land, the amount of the compensation, the person to whom it is payable, the rights of Rehabilitation and Resettlement under Chapters V and VI or the apportionment of the compensation among the persons interested:
By an order, dated 17.04.2023 in similar issue, this Court had held that in view of this particular provision which had not been examined by the District Collector, the order impugned should be set aside and fresh orders have to be passed.
opennyai_summary.19_June_2023__decision:
The time limits may be examined by the District Collector in each one of the cases and in each one of the cases that the petitioners give necessary reason for delay and if the District Collector is satisfied with the delay, then the District Collector may refer the matter to the competent Court, then the District Court at Trichy.
The said order has to be passed on the basis of the representations already given.
With respect to the period of limitation, the aforementioned directions may be followed and to avoid any technicalities, a direction is given to the petitioners herein to forward a fresh representations, copy of the original applications afresh, enclosing a copy of this order and if it is so,
within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order, then the issue of limitation need not be stressed by the District Collector.
5.In view of the above, these writ petitions are allowed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petitions are closed.

opennyai_summary.final__facts:
In the said land, one irrigation well was in existence for irrigation purpose of the said land.
In order to determine the compensation, the land under acquisition was treated as manavari dry land by the second respondent and the value as compensation was determined at Rs.66,304/- per hectare.
But in the case on hand, the petitioner's land cannot to be treated as agricultural land with irrigation facility.
Further, the respondent treated the petitioner's land at par with other adjacent lands which were classified as dry land and the same have no irrigation facilities such as open well or borewell.
5. Admittedly, the petitioner's land was compensated under the head of dry land.
As per the award dated 10.11.1999, the subject land was treated as dry land for determining compensation.
Therefore,
the Government order is not at all applicable to the case on hand.
Further, there is no separate classification as punjai land with irrigation facility or without irrigation facility in the Government order.
Court of India laid down that the compensation has to be awarded to the agricultural land taking into consideration the irrigation facility is available in that land.
However, the Government order is silent about the available irrigation facility in the form of well.

7. With the above direction, this writ petition stands allowed.
